How much flood risk is here?

FEMA rates Orleans Parish's coastal flood risk Relatively Moderate and inland flood risk Relatively High — how this county compares with others, not odds for your address.

  • Coastal flood riskRelatively Moderate
  • Inland flood riskRelatively High

This is FEMA's plain risk rating for the county, a comparison — not a prediction for your home. coastal: higher flood risk than about 63% of U.S. counties; FEMA models roughly $1,856,223 of flood loss a year across all its buildings. inland: higher flood risk than about 33% of U.S. counties; FEMA models roughly $46,671,982 of flood loss a year across all its buildings. Any loss figure is a whole-county estimate across all buildings, never one home's expected loss or premium.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective NRI 2023 release; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

Am I required to carry it?

Whether you must carry flood insurance depends on your exact address and loan — look your address up on FEMA's flood map. The rule: a federally backed mortgage on a building in a high-risk zone (a Special Flood Hazard Area) legally requires it. For context, 30.1% of Orleans Parish's existing NFIP policies sit in those high-risk (A/V) zones — not 30.1% of all buildings, and not an answer about your own home.

  • Zone X46,199 policy units
  • Zone AE17,606 policy units
  • Zone B1,350 policy units
  • Zone A01794 policy units
  • Zone A03511 policy units
  • Zone A04430 policy units
  • Zone VE268 policy units
  • Zone A02229 policy units
  • Other or unclassified zones601 policy units

Zone mix by policy units (summed policyCount). Federal rule: a lender must require flood insurance on a building in a Special Flood Hazard Area with a federally backed loan (42 U.S.C. §4012a). This is the mix of existing policies, not of all buildings, and does not establish any one property's obligation.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective July 31, 2026; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

How much does it cost here?

Among existing single-family primary-residence NFIP policies in Orleans Parish, the median annual cost is $1,093, with the middle half between $996 and $1,264 (35,924 policies). This is what current policyholders pay — a new policy on a different building can differ. Most policyholders here pay below FEMA's full “risk-based” price — what a policy would cost without today's discounts and yearly caps, about $1,095 median — the gap a bill can climb toward over time; see below.

Each policy's annual cost (premium plus fees), single-family primary residences. The bar is the middle half (p25–p75); the orange line is FEMA's full-risk price.

Coverage in force: $15,583,762,000 of building and $4,690,226,000 of contents coverage across all Orleans Parish policies.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective July 31, 2026; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

How do current premiums compare with FEMA's full-risk price?

35.6% of 35,924 single-family policies pay less than FEMA's own full-risk price; the median full-risk premium is $1,095 versus the $1,093 actually charged.

  • Median charged now$1,093
  • Median full-risk price$1,095
  • Pay below full risk35.6% of 35,924

Years to the full-risk price: under the statutory cap, premiums for most primary residences rise at most 18% a year (HFIAA cap, FEMA Risk Rating 2.0). At that maximum rate a policy at today's median ($1,093) would take at least about 1 annual renewal to reach the median full-risk price ($1,095). This is the cap on how fast a bill can climb, not a forecast of any one policy; statutory surcharges and fees are outside the cap.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective July 31, 2026; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

Can I pay less than the sticker price?

1 of Orleans Parish's 1 NFIP communities carry a Community Rating System discount — a group discount a town earns for extra flood-prevention work — that cuts every eligible policy's premium, up to 15% inside the high-risk zone (New Orleans/Orleans Parish).

CommunityCRS classHigh-risk discountOther-area discount
New Orleans/Orleans Parish715%5%

The Community Rating System cuts NFIP premiums for every eligible policy in a community that does extra flood work. The discount shown is the community's rate; what share of its policies currently receive it is not in this data. Confirm with your agent.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective October 22, 2026; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

How do I actually get covered — and how fast?

Flood damage is almost never covered by a standard homeowners policy; you buy flood insurance separately through the federal NFIP or a private insurer. Two facts change your timing and your limits:

  • Waiting period~30 days
  • NFIP building limit$250,000
  • NFIP contents limit$100,000

Most NFIP policies take effect 30 days after you buy, so you can't buy today and be covered for a storm this week — a flood-zone letter or an approaching season is a reason to act now. (Exceptions: no wait when coverage is required to close a loan, or one day after a map change puts a home in a high-risk zone.) NFIP covers up to $250,000 on the building and $100,000 on contents (contents bought separately); higher-value homes add private “excess” flood insurance. To buy: call the NFIP at 1-877-336-2627, go to FloodSmart.gov, or ask any licensed insurance agent — NFIP's price is set federally, so it is the same whichever agent you use.

Source: FEMA National Flood Insurance Program — waiting period, coverage limits and how to buy, via FloodSmart.gov. Not endorsed by FEMA.

What do floods actually pay out here?

Between 1978 and 2026, Orleans Parish had 127,255 paid NFIP flood claims totalling $7,176,275,206.

Orange bars are the three costliest years: 2005 ($6,682,687,434), 1995 ($160,406,363), 2019 ($44,436,935). Net building + contents payments by year of loss. Claims are matched by the claims dataset's county code, which may not exactly match a policy's property county.

That is 127,255 paid claims since 1978 against 67,988 policies in force today — a cumulative tally spanning ~49 years over a present-day snapshot, not an annual claim rate or a flood probability.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective 1978–2026; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

How often do the same homes flood here?

FEMA has recorded 11,447 properties in Orleans Parish that flooded more than once and drew federal disaster aid for repeat flood losses, including 150 rated severe repetitive-loss.

  • Repeat-loss properties11,447
  • Severe repetitive-loss150

FEMA-designated repetitive-loss (RL) and severe repetitive-loss (SRL) properties — individual homes with more than one flood loss over time, aggregated to the county and distinct from the annual NFIP claim counts above. A high count means the same homes flood again and again here. These drew FEMA Individual Assistance (for uninsured losses), so read it as a chronic-flooding signal, not an insured-claims total.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective 2026-10-24; retrieved 2026-10-24. FEMA repetitive-loss flood-property records. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

More data: FEMA disaster aid & reconciliation

Did the government pay homeowners after floods?

FEMA approved $969,636,774 in Individual & Households housing help to Orleans Parish homeowners across 14 disasters, on 217,168 valid registrations.

FEMA Individual Assistance is disaster aid, usually capped and partial — separate from NFIP insurance and not a substitute for a policy.

Source: FEMA OpenFEMA. Data effective owner registrations by disaster; retrieved October 22, 2026. This product uses the Federal Emergency Management Agency's OpenFEMA API, but is not endorsed by FEMA.

What this data cannot tell you

  • Your own premium — it depends on elevation, coverage and deductible. We show where existing policies fall.
  • Private (non-NFIP) flood insurance prices.
  • Your address's exact flood zone — use FEMA's Flood Map Service Center.
  • Why premiums are rising — we show the gap to full-risk, not the cause.
  • A year-over-year premium trend — the in-force snapshot holds only current-term policies, so a like-for-like multi-year index isn't possible from this data. A per-effective-year median is shown only where several years of policies exist.
